## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sampayuttakathā* (Kv 7.2) is the second discourse of the seventh chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, belonging to the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral]. Positioned between the *Saṅgahitakathā* (Kv 7.1) and the *Cetasikakathā* (Kv 7.3), the debate examines the nature of "associated" or mutually connected mental phenomena (*sampayutta*) [Hazra 1994].
In early Abhidhamma doctrinal development, the text refines the definition of association (*sampayoga* / *sampayutta*) by refuting the position that dhammas are not associated with other dhammas, establishing association through seven precise criteria: having the same origin (*ekuppāda*), cessation (*ekanirodha*), physical base (*ekavatthuka*), and object (*ekārammaṇa*), as well as being co-existent (*sahagata*), co-nascent (*sahajāta*), and conjoined (*saṃsaṭṭha*) [Qian Lin 2015]. This canonical refutation in the *Kathāvatthu* is cited in post-canonical exegesis, notably by Buddhaghosa in the *Atthasālinī* (the commentary on the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi*), to explain the meaning of *sampayutta* via shared arising and related conditions [Qian Lin 2015].
SuttaCentral records no curated cross-language parallels for the discourse and lists one translation [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus records 263 matching passages shared across 17 Pali texts, with no cross-language matches meeting the threshold of 10 [DharmaNexus]. Significant Pali-internal textual reuse occurs with the *Paṇṇattivāraniddesa* of the *Yamaka* (Ya 2.1.2), the *Khandhavibhaṅga* (Vb 1), the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, and neighboring chapters within the *Kathāvatthu* itself (notably Kv 7.1 and Kv 7.3), in addition to sharing formulas with Abhidhamma commentaries such as the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
